mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates above 4.2% signal labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns remain positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.2%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in labor force participation (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signal a synchronized economic contraction, reducing corporate profitability and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances where both PAYEMS and INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300k units signals weakening consumer demand for durable goods, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days in late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when HOUST < 1300 during late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.5% annualized signals robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of quarters with GDPC1 growth >2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Inflation exceeding 3.5% annualized (CPIAUCSL) signals monetary policy tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS coupled with declining INDPRO signals aggressive monetary tightening during supply contraction, reducing liquidity and corporate output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rates below 3.5% during post-shock recovery phases signal labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and equity returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in >40% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% during recovery phases.
